CBERG_INDEX_PATH is a base path; the actual index and its chunk-table manifest / graph sidecars are per-directory ("<base>.<roothash>[.chunks|.manifest|.graph]"). Pointing at a different tree never reuses another tree's chunks, and reverting to a prior tree finds its embeddings (and graph) still cached. Sidecars are written even in chunk-only mode when the base path is set, so warm restart can reload the graph without ONNX.

Wrap the large, frozen system prompt so the provider caches it instead of re-billing it on every tool round and every turn. Anthropic needs an explicit `cacheControl` breakpoint (1h TTL survives the gaps between turns); OpenAI caches matching prefixes automatically, so there the system prompt stays a plain string and the cache key is pinned on the request options instead. Either way the prompt text is byte-identical across calls - the precondition for any prefix cache to hit.

Fetch an http(s) URL and return its readable text. HTML is reduced to text; plain-text/JSON is passed through; other content types are reported but not decoded. Fit history to an estimated token budget, retaining recent whole exchanges. The latest exchange is always preserved, even when it alone exceeds the budget. Prior `<history_file>` tags on those turns are copied onto the new marker. If the summary still overflows, the same file list goes on an omission marker — there is no second archive pass.

this function makes sure py can run pip. SearXNG's managed install runs `python3 -m venv` then `pip install` inside it (launcher/internal/searxng). Homebrew's python formula bundles pip, so this path is apt-only in practice.

Fetch following redirects manually so each hop is re-checked against the SSRF guard. The default `redirect: "follow"` would let a public URL bounce to `http://169.254.169.254` or `localhost` unchecked — the dangerous request goes out before any final-URL inspection. Here every `Location` is validated with `assertFetchableUrl` *before* it is followed, so a redirect into a private or blocked host is refused instead of fetched.

Current rating of each rated answer in a conversation, keyed by assistant message id.

MCP servers from `mcp.json`, as a tool source. Connection failures are isolated per server so a broken config cannot take down the rest of the agent. Tools are named `mcp_<server>_<tool>` so they never collide with built-ins (this source is composed *last*, and collectTools also first-wins). The tools are registered here, but the agent withholds them from the model until `load_mcp_tools` activates the ones a turn needs. Full descriptions and argument schemas are written under the context store, one folder per server, so they are not inlined into every prompt.

`run_script` executes model-written Python that calls the same read-only tools `batch` may run, so dependent lookups, loops and filtering happen in one step and only the printed summary enters the transcript. Scripts have no call, output or default time limit; long ones run as background jobs the agent can check and cancel. With `output_to_file`, printed output is streamed to a context file instead of being returned. `tools` must be the unwrapped, unjournaled tool set: scripts receive full results, and a script making 100k calls must not write 100k run records.
Validate data at the settings HTTP boundary before using it as render state.

this function returns the single, idempotent teardown: release the search service (cancelling an in-flight install), then SIGTERM the daemon's process group, SIGKILL if it overstays. The daemon's signal handler stops the supervisor, which interrupts cberg-index. exited closes once the daemon is gone.
Sends texts and reads back count L2-normalized vectors.

Imports each ready file in turn; files that are not ready or fail stay in `remaining`. Stops when aborted.
Moves the walked leaves, sorted by path, into m's entries and meta.
Wraps the child's pipes as unbuffered input and buffered output streams. Takes ownership of pid and both fds either way.

Assign each row to a group keyed by its body. A 64-bit hash-prefix hit is confirmed against the full hash; a mismatch (collision) or an all-zero prefix (the map reserves key 0) just starts its own group. The map records only the first group for a prefix, so a collision leaves the original mapping intact.
Vector-searches one repo. Filtered searches oversample and keep doubling the fetch until k hits pass or the index runs out.
this function tries to install a missing requirement and reports whether its check passes afterward.
A protocol request, or undefined for any other stdout line.

Converts the module path between the crate and the symbol ("a::b") into a file path ("a/b"). Returns its length, or -1 when it does not fit.
this function maps every canonical key to its resolved value (after all layers). It is the single list of keys the launcher reads besides passthroughKeys.
Starts `python script backend model` with pipes to its stdin and from its stdout. On success *to_fd and *from_fd are the parent's ends.
this function reports whether SearXNG could be installed here (a host python exists).

A scheduled wake-up reads as a timeline event, not a user bubble; its prompt stays collapsed.

Cheap, current execution state for the UI activity indicator.
Capture the tree as the baseline the next restart diffs against.

Confidence of a ref bound to a known node: same-file bindings rank below import-resolved ones, which rank below exact ones.
this function wraps out. Without animate, statuses print as a single plain line, which suits pipes, log files and dumb terminals.
Parses a hit's id and score values (located by json_object_read_key).
Parses a successful JSON body, or throws the response's {@link HttpError}.
Stable UTC date keys make daily requests durable and idempotent after restart.
The caller supplies the configured Codeberg home, never a browser path.
this function splits a command string into per-stage argv lists.
this function maps each per-root tag (".<16 hex>") to the total size of its files.
An opt-in flag: only an explicit "on" spelling enables it.
this function locates a system python3 (preferred) or python interpreter.

Resolve the configured web-search backend, or `undefined` when none is set — in which case `web_search` stays unregistered and `fetch_url` still works. Today only SearXNG (selected by `CODEBERG_SEARXNG_URL`); a second backend is one more adapter plus a branch here.
this function splits on newlines; a final newline does not add an empty line.
this function splits formatted log lines on fieldSep into field slices.
Indexed repositories passed internally by the launcher or project catalog.

Carry over every chunk except those of `rechunk`+`deleted`, re-chunk `rechunk` from disk, and sync the union — so only the affected files are parsed and only chunks whose content moved get re-embedded. Graph drops for deleted / emptied paths run after repo_sync_chunks (table + fragment apply) and before repo_sync_vectors, so a vector failure cannot leave stale graph nodes for paths already removed from the chunk table, and a failed parse or chunk sync cannot drop graph state ahead of the table. Fills batch with every unchanged chunk plus the re-chunked files, and lists in graph_drop the paths that lose their graph nodes: deleted files and files that no longer yield chunks. graph_drop borrows the caller's strings and needs room for rechunk_n + deleted_n entries.
Full tool output the model was not shown inline. The path is a hash of the body, so the same output is one file. `tools/INDEX.txt` gains a line only when that file is created.
this function lists provider keys in name order, values masked.
this function are shown only when they differ from the default.
Searches every repo with one query vector and keeps the k best hits by score. Repos that are not ready are skipped; if none is, NOT_FOUND.
Wipe the vectors and every sidecar derived from them, so the repo cold-reindexes from source.

Config files in merge order (later overrides the same server name): `~/.codeberg/mcp.json`, then each indexed root's `.cursor/mcp.json` and `.codeberg/mcp.json`, then `CODEBERG_MCP_CONFIG`. When no indexed roots are set, the git project (or cwd) is used instead of cwd itself — the launcher sets cwd to the codeberg checkout, which is not the repo being indexed.
Offline inspection/decisions need no model; only planning resolves provider credentials.
this function boots the daemon, waits for health, runs the browser UI, and cleans up. Launcher status goes to term; the browser UI keeps writing to the terminal.

Loads the index at path when it exists, else creates an empty one. An existing file keeps its saved scalar kind; the config only applies to newly created indexes (migration = rebuild). opts->quantization reports the kind in use.
A report and its decision receipts form one age-filtered knowledge revision family.
Resolve a tool only after its outcome is durable; a missing outcome remains uncertain.
Releases status and reports whether the ORT call succeeded.
Copies a capture's text, truncated to CBERG_GRAPH_NAME_MAX. For imports, strips one layer of quotes / angle brackets and trims rust use-tree braces ("x::{a, b}" -> "x").
Reads the next leaf into m. A truncated or corrupt leaf is NOT_FOUND, which makes the caller start cold.
Mirrors `attemptForMessage` + `currentFeedback` for every message at once.
Reconcile a crash between writing the new state and deleting the old file.
Processes one line (len excludes the newline and a trailing CR).
this function renders a byte count compactly.
A new assistant answer as an attempt to build; repository versions are read only when one exists.

this function makes sure a python3 **with a working pip** is available for the SearXNG web-search backend, auto-installing what's missing via the host package manager when possible. It is intentionally separate from Ensure (the build prerequisites): web search is an optional runtime feature, so callers treat a returned error as advisory and degrade gracefully (web_search off, everything else on).
Reads a request body, refusing more than `maxBytes` with a 413. The rest of an oversized body is drained so the response can still be delivered.
Line-oriented chunking for YAML and TOML: each boundary line starts a chunk named after it; content before the first boundary is an unnamed preamble.
this function checks one pipeline stage against the read-only allowlist.
Records one inotify event: the changed path as dirty, and a new subdirectory as something to start watching.
Splits buf in place on '/'; false when there are too many segments.
Finds the node a trace starts from by name. path_prefix narrows the candidates; a node whose file is exactly that path wins.

this function resolves the embedding model and the vector index built from it. Both default under the managed home (not the repo) so the model is downloaded once and the index survives repo moves, re-clones, and rebuilds. Paths are stored absolute so the daemon resolves them regardless of cwd.
Explicit close, Settings off, chat/project deletion, and shutdown share cleanup.
Separate read failures from write results; stale reads never replace a newer selection.

Merge tool sources in order. Earlier sources win on a name collision, so a later source (e.g. the daemon's dynamic tools, or web tools) can never shadow a core tool. This is the single place that defines the agent's tool-merge policy.
this function builds the environment overlay for the Node agent.
Nearest ancestor of `cwd` that contains `.git`, or `cwd` itself.

Wrap a loop so each call's messages pass through `transforms` in order before reaching the model. This module owns the awkward knowledge that a call carries its transcript as either `messages` or an array `prompt` (and that a string `prompt` has no transcript to touch) — callers just supply transforms. It is the seam shared by prompt hooks and history compaction: a new cross-cutting rewrite is one more transform, not another hand-rolled Proxy.
Adds one reference. References with an invalid endpoint, or one that did not resolve to a live chunk, are dropped.
this function returns the package name for r under pm, or "" if pm can't install it.
Providers the catalog names, whether or not their credentials are set.
this function waits for a free connection slot on socket or for ctx to end.
this function returns the last complete line, or the unfinished one after it.
Keep the daemon pure Go: macOS process counters come from one bounded ps call.
this function notes why the indexer stopped and returns how long to wait before starting it again. A requested replacement restarts at once and is not a failure.

this function reports whether the managed install is complete: the venv and source checkout exist AND the dependencies finished installing (the `.ready` marker). A half-finished install — e.g. the checkout cloned but `pip install` failed — reports false so the next run retries it.
Lay the rows out so a representative and all its duplicates are contiguous in `members`, letting each embed window be freed before the next.
Moves the staged paths to the caller's events (or bare paths) array; the caller then owns them.

this function resolves a user-given repo list — directory paths and/or registry keys — into entries, preserving input order and deduping by resolved root. A directory is registered via Upsert unless register is false, in which case an unregistered path gets a session-only entry (basename key, disambiguated within the selection) and the registry file is not touched; an already-registered path reuses its registered key either way. A key must name a registered repo whose root still exists. Paths win over keys when an item could be read as both.
Builds next from incoming against the live table: added and modified rows from incoming, deletes from unseen live rows, then the new fingerprint.

Chunks a root JSON object into one chunk per top-level key (span = key through its value, bracket- and string-aware). Sets *out_handled = 0 when the root is not an object or parsing fails so the caller can fall back to window chunks. JSONC comments are skipped; trailing non-whitespace after the root object is emitted as one unnamed chunk.
One-line header for hybrid hits (final score + optional lexical boost).
Tombstone a file's nodes/refs without compacting (used by transactional apply).
Migrates retryable jobs failed by older one-shot queue policies back to pending.

Chunk (and, when the repo has a graph, extract) one file. out_frag may be NULL to skip extraction; a NULL *out_frag with OK means the file carries no graph structure (markdown, config, unknown language, or unreadable). Only running out of memory is an error. A file that cannot be read or parsed is skipped with a warning and reported like an empty one. Reads a source file into *out_data. Oversized, vanished, or unreadable files leave *out_data NULL and are skipped (with a warning unless the file simply vanished); only running out of memory is an error.
this function lists the cached index sets and (unless DryRun) removes them.
The agent for one chat turn, plus a step callback that records the turn's token usage under the selected model (or the step's own model when the request carries no selection).
Form fields that start over for each selected example or permission change.
this function starts codeberg-d in its own process group, writing both of its output streams to out.
Run the prelude + script, serving tool requests until the process exits.
this function starts the indexer again. A start that fails is retried like any other exit rather than leaving the project without an indexer for good.
Undefined when `allNames` has no deferred MCP tools.
The recorded owner is gone, or no owner was recorded and the lock is old.
this function canonicalizes an explicitly selected repository key.
Local submitted chats remain reachable even when their first save fails.
Reads the chosen files and asks the server what each readable one would import as.
Appends one formatted header line to req; false when it does not fit.

Follow repository-relative citations, never an arbitrary path from model output.
Runs the trace on a locked, ready repo and converts the hops.
The web shell and setup documentation are usable before model setup.
All saved chats, newest first. Network/parse errors yield an empty list.
this function stops the writer before removing caches. Retained data uses the same stable directory when roots are added again; source repositories are untouched.
Parses "in", "out", or "both" (the default) into graph direction flags.
this function is called only by the dedicated, bounded disk loop, never HTTP handlers.
A `.catch` handler: a missing file or directory yields `fallback`; other errors are rethrown.
this function anchors only word-character edges: \b beside a leading "--", "@" or "$" demands a word character before it, so " --flag" never matched.

Every tool the daemon advertises over `/tools`, bridged to ai-sdk dynamic tools. The daemon owns the catalogue and the execution; this adapter only maps its schema and forwards calls — so the daemon can add tools without any agent change.
Caller owns embed_mu, except during single-threaded engine setup. Lock order is repo->mu before embed_mu; never acquire a repo lock here.
Counts FILE nodes by language, from their path extensions.
The block between the opening and closing `---` fences.
Close incomplete protocol exchanges without claiming their external outcome is known.
Returns the listening fd, or -1 with nothing left behind.
A def index is either -1 (the file node) or within the fragment's defs.
Normalize OpenAI arrays and System One maps without inventing missing probabilities.

this function registers root, resolving it to its real absolute path first (the path is the repo's identity — a symlinked alias maps to the same entry). An already-registered root returns its existing entry unchanged; a new one is appended under its basename, disambiguated with a short path-hash suffix when another repo already claimed that name.
Tokens the budgets below are fractions of: the window, capped by `workingWindow`.
One bad file must not cost the project its index: say which file was left out and why, then carry on. Capped so a tree of them cannot flood the log.
this function reports whether py's pip module is usable — the actual thing a venv created from it needs, which a bare `python3` binary check doesn't confirm.
Reads one node record into g. A truncated or corrupt record is NOT_FOUND, which makes the caller rebuild the graph cold.
Returns the index just past one member value starting at i: at the top-level ',' that ends it, at the root '}', or after its closing bracket.
The agent uses ai-sdk v7's timed tool loop, which merges abort signals via AbortSignal.any. Fail at startup rather than after the user's first message.
Waits up to timeout_ms for events (0 polls without blocking and is not a timeout), then drains every queued event.
Diff the saved tree against a fresh rebuild (stat-only for unchanged files) and re-chunk only what changed. On success *out_current is the fresh tree, owned by the caller.
Paths are passed as an argument or environment value, never script source.
Cache annotations are transport metadata. Business data inside tool inputs and JSON outputs, including fields named providerOptions, remains significant.
Rejects after `timeoutMs` even when the request ignores its abort signal.

`run_script` is opt-in: it executes model-written Python on this machine. - `CODEBERG_SCRIPT_USE=true` registers the tool. - `CODEBERG_SCRIPT_PYTHON` overrides the interpreter (default `python3`, or `python` on Windows).
Rename rather than copy durable queues and datasets. Interrupted upgrades resume each missing source independently. Never overwrite a destination.

Only an unwatchable root fails registration. A subdirectory the platform cannot watch (inotify needs read access) is left out, matching the walk: one locked folder must not stop the rest of the tree from being watched.
Loads the settings; `active` tells a late save whether this load is still the current one.
this function is the KEY=VALUE config file inside Home.
Expand Cursor/VS Code style `${env:NAME}`, `${workspaceFolder}`, `${userHome}`.
this function is value with a built-in default.
Undefined while summaries follow the chat model (the default).
this function downloads the default ONNX model with scripts/fetch-model.sh into the launcher-owned model dir (the parent of EmbedModel), which lives under ~/.codeberg rather than the repo.
this function returns the IndexerError if err wraps one.
this function executes a validated read-only pipeline rooted at dir.
String fields from a YAML map. Aliases are rejected, so a skill cannot expand one.
Pick a ready repo for graph queries. Explicit key must exist; otherwise the first ready repo with a live graph wins (single-repo default).
A live node of an allowed kind, inside the graph's repo scope and under the path prefix. A zero kind mask and an empty prefix each match everything.
this function is the base this function the agent's web_search should call.
this function migrates local caches before the initial indexer starts. A remote store retains its namespace to avoid silently rebuilding into another table.
Graph extraction reuses the chunking parse tree (ADR 0005: one parse pass feeds both indexes). The extractor is created on first use.
this function connects to socket, retrying while its backlog is full (other processes can still fill it) until ctx ends.
Open every root listed in CODEBERG_ROOTS (newline-separated records).
Before the total is known the indexer reports how many files it has read.
What the workspace chrome needs from the active chat. Unlike `useChat`, it re-renders on status changes and the first message, not on every streamed token.
this function locates codeberg's own files: a source checkout or a prebuilt install.
Bound retained DOM without disposing independently running conversations.
Forward refs bound directly to this node, from live sources.

Open one repo under the engine: per-root chunk table, watcher, and (in vector mode) the "<base>.<roothash>" index + sidecars — the exact single-root layout, so existing on-disk indexes stay valid. `root` must already be resolved.

usearch v2.25.3's built-in i8 cosine (metric_cos_i8_t) returns distance 0 — a perfect match — whenever the integer dot product is exactly 0, i.e. for orthogonal vectors; the zero guard belongs on the norms (as in the f32 template). Until upstream ships a fix, i8 indexes get this corrected metric, registered through usearch_change_metric with the dimension as the callback state (stateful metrics are invoked as f(a, b, state)).
Earliest pending retry or abandoned lease, including a claim with no lease.
Removes a socket file left behind by a dead indexer (it refuses connections). Returns -1 when the path is not a socket, something still answers on it, or it cannot be removed.
Rough, provider-independent estimate used to decide when to compact.
Tombstones path's live nodes, recording their slots in u->node_idx.
Canvas data stays private to the user: new directories are created 0700.
Until a usable chat model exists, every page except the canvas is documentation.
True when the stack/response cap may have clipped results the caller asked for.

Rows per ORT Run (CBERG_EMBED_BATCH, 1..MAX_BATCH). Inputs are length-sorted first, so this trades per-Run overhead against the padding of each group. On CPU, 8-16 rows beat 32+ (bench_embed); accelerators may prefer larger runs.
Takes ownership of every event's path, also on failure.

Inclusive end index for a branch. Out-of-range values clamp into the transcript; a user prompt followed by an assistant reply snaps forward so the copy is a complete turn rather than a dangling question.
this function builds a one-repo workspace (key "main" is the default).
this function reports whether f is a terminal that can redraw a status line.
The provider boundary sees system text, active tool schemas, normalized attachments and each tool step. Recovery here never replays tool execution.
Inspect background results; execution is driven by review and runtime reconciliation.
Get-or-create the module node an import points at.
Change-list rows are shallow copies: content_hash/id by value, strings borrow the table arena (valid until the next sync commits a new arena).

SearXNG (open-source, self-hosted, no API key) as a web-search backend. The instance must have the JSON output format enabled (`search.formats: [html, json]`). All of SearXNG's quirks — the `/search` path, the `format=json` query, the result shape — are contained here.
Builds (but does not start) the HTTP server. Call `.listen()` to run it.
this function executes a git command in dir with a 30s timeout (interactive tool use).
A directory import's entrypoint: index.<ext>, __init__.py, or mod.rs, if exactly one exists.
Loads the saved-chat list and exposes a `refresh` to re-pull it (after a save or delete). Errors are swallowed in `listSessions`, so this never throws.
The FILE node for path: the exact qname match, else the first candidate; 0 when there is none. Looked up afresh each time since compaction may have moved nodes.
this function returns the key a line assigns (whether active `KEY=...` or a commented `# KEY=...` template line), or "" if the line is not an assignment.
Re-chunk what the diff added or modified and drop what it deleted. The diff's paths borrow from the manifests it compared; both must outlive this call.

this function launches the managed SearXNG and waits (bounded) for it to answer. preferredPort is used when free, otherwise a free ephemeral port is chosen. logw receives the instance's stdout/stderr. Returns an error (caller degrades to a warning) if it can't start or never becomes ready.
Reads and parses models.yml once so the model and decision catalogs can share it.
Map Rust sources by path / crate:: segments (Cargo.toml crate name is not remapped).
Collects the ids of every FILE node. Ids, not node pointers: rewriting an import may compact and free graph->nodes. *out_ids is caller-freed.
The unfiltered sidebar list runs after every save, so it re-reads only chats whose files changed since the last listing (other processes included).
Pull citeable code locations from a daemon tool result for sources/ledger.
Picks the current learning choice at job execution time, including recovered jobs.
Tombstones path's live refs, recording their slots in u->ref_idx.
Every non-archived artifact plus which ones are current, from one projection.
Strict: a corrupt spend record is reported, never silently dropped.
Emits the open section, titled by the breadcrumb when under a heading.

Background learning shares the chat path's working window: a 1M-token model must not be sent a half-window prompt (long-context premium included) for one extraction. CODEBERG_CONTEXT_BUDGET raises the ceiling for both.

Best-effort "main content" isolation: prefer a `<main>` region, else the largest `<article>`, else drop the common chrome elements (nav/header/footer aside) wholesale. Heuristic — good enough to cut boilerplate from docs and articles without a DOM parser; pages with none of these are returned as-is.
One line per chunk ([repo] path:lines symbol), most recent first. Bounded to `max` rows. Returns null when empty so callers can skip injection.
All sessions, newest first. Corrupt/unreadable files are skipped.
Takes work_mu then r->mu, so searches see either the old or the new state.
A successful POST stays confirmed even if the following dashboard GET fails.
this function returns the resolved value for a recognized key (after all layers), and whether the key is recognized. Useful for `config get`.

YAML boundary: a column-0 `key:` mapping line (colon followed by space/tab or end of line, quotes respected, comments ignored). Indented lines, list items, comments, and `---` separators are never boundaries, so nested content stays inside its top-level key's chunk. Index of the first `:` that ends a mapping key (followed by space, tab, or end of line), skipping quoted text and stopping at a comment; len when there is none.
An identical ordered set needs neither a replacement arena nor a fingerprint sort. Comparing unique live keys in order also rejects incoming duplicates.
Refreshes the dashboard every five seconds while a report is being produced.
Context files for one user (`$CODEBERG_HOME/context`). Stable across runs so a resumed chat can still open the history file named in its summary.
Use the normal resume lifecycle so failures, active turns and drafts stay local.
The deleted dialog and trigger disappear; move focus to a surviving control.
What the workspace shows about the server: its title, learning switches, and the chat model's inputs.

this function combines independently retrieved vector chunks and lexical lines using reciprocal ranks. A grep line inside a vector chunk reinforces that chunk; otherwise it remains a citeable, lexical-only hit (id=0) for read_file.

this function verifies the executable that will actually run the agent. Merely finding `node` on PATH is insufficient: older Nodes start the web server but ai-sdk's timed first request then crashes at AbortSignal.any.
Reference walk, used when no cache is available for this file.
`run_script`: the Python the agent wrote and what it printed.
TOML boundary: a `[table]` / `[[array-of-tables]]` header line.
Resolve at tool execution: pooled agents can serve several concurrent chats.
Keep one SDK stream alive across transport failures so text/tool parser state is retained.
Browser journals and CLI asks own fresh caches; pooled agents share no results across runs.
Writes the header, then every live node and ref.
Request options for a JSON body.
Keep page boundaries between complete UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

Resolve MCP config from the environment and mcp.json files. Missing files are not an error; invalid files become warnings. User servers are disabled via `CODEBERG_MCP_USE=false`. The built-in database server is separate and off unless `CODEBERG_DBMCP_USE` is set; it is registered only when a spec file and the `dbmcp` binary are both present. A later mcp.json entry named `databases` replaces that built-in command.
The one repo whose Rust crate is named by the import's first segment, or SIZE_MAX when none or several are.
this function tells the indexer which model to embed with and, for models that do not run on ONNX, which worker process to start.
A timeout the agent asked for, in milliseconds; none means run until done.

Anthropic only caches up to an explicit breakpoint, and the system prompt is the only one `cachedInstructions` sets. Without more, every tool round re-bills the whole transcript (all earlier tool results) at the full input rate. Mark two rolling breakpoints on the transcript tail: - the last message, which writes this step's prefix to the cache; - the message that ended the previous step (just before the latest assistant turn), which reads what the previous step wrote even when a step adds more blocks than the provider's lookback window. Together with the system breakpoint that is 3 of Anthropic's 4. Other cache strategies return the input unchanged.

Reads the project list for a page load. The projects seldom change, so when the daemon is busy or restarting the last list it reported is served at once; project status polling reports the underlying problem separately.
this function runs stop when the launcher receives SIGTERM. SIGINT is consumed and left to the foreground child. The returned function ends the subscription.

JSON strings may not carry raw control characters; the daemon's decoder rejects the whole response if one slips through (form feeds in C sources, ANSI escapes in logs). Escapes are never split when out fills up.
Cross-process lock. A crashed owner's lock is recovered; a live owner's is never taken over.

The system prompt, optionally extended with web-tools and MCP sections. Kept as a pure function of the enabled capabilities so the cached prefix is byte-stable for a given configuration: when web use is off and no MCP servers connected the prompt is exactly `AGENT_SYSTEM`, and the `web_search` line appears only when a search backend is configured — so the model is never told about a tool that isn't registered.
this function annotates the (unset) external SearXNG URL to make clear the launcher manages a local instance when web use is on and none is set.
this function lists everything `make build-daemon` + `make build-agent` need.
Human controls span all chats of the selected project; agent tools stay chat-scoped.
Fills hash with the file's body hash, reusing the previous manifest's when size and mtime are unchanged. Returns CBERG_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the file cannot be read, which skips it.
Prefixed MCP tool names already present as calls or results.
JSON-ish rendering of a tool payload. Falls back to String when the value cannot be serialized (cycles, bigint).
Installation and startup run only after Settings or explicit configuration opts into search. The UI can cancel either operation without a restart.
this function checks the fields required to actually launch.
Providers whose OpenAI Responses API accepts `reasoningEffort: 'max'`.
Divides the copied transcript from what this branch adds after it.
All resolved edges arriving at `rec`'s node.
this function performs the uninstall against the resolved config.
this function encodes the served repos as newline-separated "key\tpath" records, the CODEBERG_ROOTS wire format. Empty when no roots are set.
Builds the directory node for leaves [lo, hi), whose paths share the first prefix bytes. Returns NULL and sets *err on failure.
A short, file-safe id, within the server's `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` guard.
Loads the server's slash-command catalog once for the composer autocomplete.

Mix the key before masking: chunk ids are sequential, and the low bits of sequential keys would cluster badly under linear probing modulo a power of two. splitmix64 finalizer scatters them across the table.
Bring the vector index in line with one chunk-table sync, then save it.
Interactive opens must distinguish a missing chat from a failed request.
